'''Douglas Richard "Doug" McDermott''' (born January 3, 1992) is an American [[basketball]] player who plays for the Charlotte Hornets of the NBA.
. He led the nation in scoring in 2013–14, was a consensus first team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] in 2012, 2013, and 2014, and scored the fifth-most points in NCAA Division I men's basketball history. He was also named to the team that represented the United States in the [[2011 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]]. He is the son of his coach at [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]], [[Greg McDermott]].

==High school==
McDermott, a 6'8" 215 pound [[Forward (basketball)|forward]], played high school basketball at [[Ames High School]] in [[Ames, Iowa]] alongside high school All-American [[Harrison Barnes]].  Ames won 53 consecutive games during McDermott's and Barnes' junior and senior seasons and won consecutive [[Iowa]] state titles.  As a senior, McDermott averaged 20.1 [[points per game|points]] and 7.8 [[rebounds per game]] and was named first team All-State.<ref name=BIO>{{cite web| title = Creighton bio| publisher = Creighton Athletics| year = 2013 | url = http://www.gocreighton.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=1000&ATCLID=204987431| accessdate = June 19, 2014}}</ref>

==College career==
Originally, McDermott signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play with [[Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball|Northern Iowa]], but after his father moved from coaching [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State University]] to Creighton, he was released from his commitment in order to play for him in college.

As a freshman in [[2010–11 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|2010–11]], McDermott averaged 14.9 points and 7.2 rebounds per game as he started all 39 games for the Bluejays.  McDermott set a [[Missouri Valley Conference]] (MVC) record for points by a freshman (581) and was named conference freshman and newcomer of the year.  McDermott also became the first player to earn first team all-conference honors as a freshman since Cleo Littleton of [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]] in 1954.<ref>{{cite web| title = Weems is Larry Bird Player of the Year| publisher = Missouri Valley Conference| year = 2011 | url =http://www.mvc-sports.com/mbasketball/news/2010-11/5114/weems-is-larry-bird-player-of-the-year/| accessdate = January 4, 2012}}</ref>  McDermott led the Bluejays to the [[2011 College Basketball Invitational]], where they made it to the best of three final series, ultimately losing to [[2010–11 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]].<ref name=BIO/>

Prior to his sophomore season, McDermott was named to the preseason watch lists for the [[Wooden Award]]<ref>{{cite web| title = John R. Wooden Award Announces Men’s Preseason Top 50 List| publisher = Wooden Award| year = 2011 | url =http://www.woodenaward.com/?p=1105| accessdate = December 30, 2011}}</ref> and [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Award]].<ref>{{cite web| title = 2011–12 Naismith Trophy Preseason Watch List| publisher = Slam Magazine| year = 2011 | url =http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/college/2011/11/2011-12-naismith-trophy-preseason-watch-list/| accessdate = December 30, 2011}}</ref>

As a sophomore, McDermott was one of five men named first team All-America for the 2011–12 season. McDermott is Creighton's first player honored by the NABC on its first-team All-America squad. McDermott also was named the [[Missouri Valley Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Missouri Valley Conference Player of the Year]], the first Creighton player since [[Booker Woodfox]] in 2009. McDermott finished his 2011–12 season averaging 22.9 points per game, a figure that ranked third nationally. His 801 points, 307 field goals and 48.6 percent shooting accuracy from three-point range were all school records for a single-season.  Creighton finished 29–6 and advanced to the third-round of the NCAA Tournament. On March 26, 2012, McDermott was named a first-team AP [[All American]].<ref>{{cite web| title = NABC Names Doug McDermott First Team All-American| url = http://www.gocreighton.com/ViewArticle.dbmlSPSID=89381&SPID=69&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=1000&ATCLID=205400797| accessdate = March 23, 2012}}</ref>

As a junior in 2012–13, McDermott ranked first in the nation in points scored and second in points per game. He set school records for points in a single season and points in a career. He was again named a first team All-American by the AP.<ref name=BIO/>

On April 25, 2013, McDermott announced he would be returning to Creighton for his senior season and would not be entering the [[2013 NBA Draft]].<ref>[http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2013/04/25/creightons-doug-mcdermott-announces-his-return-skips-nba/2113313/ Creighton's Doug McDermott announces his return]</ref> That July, he relinquished his scholarship and became a [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-on]] for his final season at Creighton. This came about after the NCAA had granted senior guard Grant Gibbs, who had missed full seasons at both [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] and Creighton with injuries, a rare sixth year of eligibility, putting Creighton over the NCAA's limit of 13 scholarships in the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/9444744/grant-gibbs-creighton-bluejays-gets-sixth-year-eligibility |title=Grant Gibbs granted sixth year |first=Jeff |last=Goodman |publisher=''[[ESPN.com]]'' |date=July 2, 2013 |accessdate=August 19, 2013}}</ref>

On February 28, McDermott was named one of the 10 semi-finalists for [[Naismith College Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Top 10 National Semifinalists Named for 2014 Men's Naismith Trophy presented by AT&T |url=http://naismithawards.com/PressBox/ArticleView/tabid/209/ArticleId/12/2014-Mens-Naismith-Trophy-presented-by-AT-T-Top-10-National-Semifinalists.aspx|work=Naismith Awards|accessdate=February 18, 2014|date=February 28, 2014}}</ref> On Senior Night against Providence, he scored a career-high 45 points and passed the 3,000 point threshold.<ref>{{cite news|last=Norlander|first=Matt|title=McDermott breaks 3,000 points, scores career-high 45 on Senior Night|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24473926/creightons-doug-mcdermott-makes-history-reaches-3000-career-points|accessdate=March 9, 2014|newspaper=CBS Sports|date=March 9, 2014}}</ref> McDermott was named first-team All-[[Big East Conference|Big East]] in Creighton's first season in the league.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.bigeast.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030914aaa.html |title=All-BIG EAST Men's Basketball Team Announced |publisher=Big East Conference |date=March 10, 2014 |accessdate=March 10, 2014}}</ref> He won the Big East Player of the Year award, as well as earning First-Team All-American honors by U.S. Basketball Writers Association for the third time.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.ketv.com/sports/creighton-extended-coverage/creightons-doug-mcdermott-named-big-east-player-of-the-year/24942866|title=Creighton's Doug McDermott named BIG EAST Player of the Year|publisher=KETA Omaha|date=March 12, 2014|accessdate=March 12, 2014}}</ref> McDermott was also the consensus national player of the year, winning all major awards ([[John R. Wooden Award|Wooden]],<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.woodenaward.com/?p=1693 |title=Creighton’s McDermott Wins John R. Wooden Award Presented By Wendy’s |publisher=[[Los Angeles Athletic Club]] |date=April 4, 2014 |accessdate=April 4, 2014}}</ref> [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith]],<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.naismithawards.com/PressBox/ArticleView/tabid/209/ArticleId/20/McDermott-Named-2014-Naismith-Mens-College-Player-of-the-Year-presented-by-AT-T.aspx |title=McDermott Named 2014 Naismith Men's College Player of the Year, presented by AT&T |publisher=Atlanta Tipoff Club |date=April 6, 2014 |accessdate=April 6, 2014}}</ref> [[Associated Press College Basketball Player of the Year|AP]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/10723164/creighton-doug-mcdermott-shockers-gregg-marshall-honored |title=McDermott, Marshall honored by AP |publisher=''ESPN.com'' |date=April 3, 2014 |accessdate=April 3, 2014}}</ref> [[NABC Player of the Year|NABC]],<ref>[http://static.psbin.com/e/v/f7nkpzc1p2vxt4/2014_NABC_Coaches-_POY_release.pdf Doug McDermott earns Sporting News' Player of the Year]. ''The Sporting News.'' Retrieved on March 11, 2014.</ref> [[Oscar Robertson Trophy|USBWA]],<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2014/oscar140404.html |title=Creighton's McDermott Wins 2013–14 Oscar Robertson Trophy |publisher=[[United States Basketball Writers Association]] |date=April 4, 2014 |accessdate=April 5, 2014}}</ref> and ''[[Sporting News Men's College Basketball Player of the Year|Sporting News]]''<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2014-03-11/doug-mcdermott-sporting-news-player-of-year-creighton-bluejays-3000-points-greg |title=Doug McDermott earns Sporting News Player of the Year |first=Roger |last=Kuznia |publisher=''[[Sporting News]]'' |date=March 12, 2014 |accessdate=April 6, 2014}}</ref>).

McDermott led the nation in scoring at 26.9 points per game.<ref>[http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/statistics/player/_/stat/scoring-per-game/sort/avgPoints/seasontype/2 "2013-14 NCAA Division I College Basketball Player Statistics"]. espn.go.com. Retrieved March 31, 2014.</ref> At the end of his college career, he ranked fifth on the all-time NCAA Division I scoring list, with 3,150 points.<ref>[http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/doug-mcdermott-1.html "Doug McDermott Stats"]. sports-reference.com. Retrieved March 23, 2014.</ref> He became the first player in 29 years to be named to the AP All-America first team three times.<ref>[http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/10702957/doug-mcdermott-unanimous-choice-ap-all-america-team "Doug McDermott makes 3rd AP team"]. espn.go.com. March 31, 2014. Retrieved March 31, 2014.</ref> McDermott is one of three players in NCAA men's basketball history to have 3,000 points and 1,000 rebounds. He also set an NCAA record by scoring in double figures in 135 games.<ref name=BIO/>

==Professional career==
McDermott is projected as a first-round pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]].<ref>[http://insider.espn.go.com/nba/draft/results/players/news/_/id/19767/doug-mcdermott "Doug McDermott"]. insider.espn.go.com. June 4, 2014. Retrieved June 19, 2014.</ref>

==International career==
Following the close of his freshman year at Creighton, McDermott was selected to the U. S. team sent to [[Riga]], [[Latvia]] for the 2011 [[FIBA Under-19 World Championship]].  McDermott started all nine matches and averaged 11.3 points per game on .501 shooting and 6.1 rebounds per contest, good for third on the team in both categories.  The United States finished 7–2, good for fifth in the tournament.<ref>{{cite web| title = Tenth FIBA U19 World Championship 2011| publisher = USA Basketball| year = 2011 | url =http://www.usabasketball.com/mens/u19/mu19_2011.html| accessdate = January 4, 2012}}</ref>
